title: Automating Medicare Enrollment & CMS Audits with Autonomous Multi-Agent Swarms
excerpt: How I codified nine years of real-world Medicare Advantage operations into an autonomous multi-agent mesh running inside agy and omp CLIs with zero-tolerance CMS compliance gates.
author: Prashanth Kadasi
insights: Direct codification of 9 years in enterprise Medicare Advantage operations and CMS regulatory auditing into autonomous agentic pipelines.
content:
In the Medicare Advantage (MA-PD, D-SNP, PDP) space, a single operational error is not just a bug — it can mean an elderly beneficiary losing life-sustaining prescription drug coverage on the 1st of the month, or an insurer facing statutory fines and sanction audit findings during annual CMS reviews.

The Real-World Medicare Enrollment Problem

Having spent nine years working in high-volume federal Medicare operations — starting as a Claims Associate and advancing to Enrollment Quality & Audit Representative (CMS Auditor) — I lived the daily pressure of enforcing zero-tolerance statutory compliance against Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) regulations.

The operational workflow has always suffered from severe asynchronous friction:

  • Multi-Channel Intake: Senior beneficiaries submitting either paper applications (beset by low-resolution scanner noise, misread digits, smudged checkboxes, or handwritten P.O. Box entries) or electronic portal applications with mismatched election periods.
  • Clearinghouse & MARx Adjudication: Ingestion systems translating data into CMS Record Type 61 transactions and ANSI ASC X12 EDI 834 envelopes, followed by federal adjudication returning cryptic Transaction Reply Codes (TRCs) like TRC 011 (Accepted), TRC 015 (Beneficiary Not Found), TRC 038 (Out of Service Area), or TRC 107 (P.O. Box physical residency violation).
  • Statutory 10-Day TAT Work Baskets: Any transaction fallout enters work baskets. Under CMS guidelines, items have a statutory 10-calendar-day Turnaround Time (TAT). Specialists must pull the oldest items first to prevent catastrophic regulatory SLA breaches.
  • Zero-Tolerance Quality Gates: An independent audit layer inspecting 100% of transactions, ensuring specialist remediations are substantiated by documentation and that statutory model notices (Acceptance, Denial with §50.1 appeal rights, 21-day RFI) are dispatched on time.

The Autonomous Multi-Agent Mesh Architecture

I built MediFlow to automate and mathematically audit this entire lifecycle using seven coordinated autonomous AI agents powered by Google Antigravity (agy) and omp runtimes with Gemini models:

  • Maya (Paper Ingestion OCR Agent): Simulates mailroom scanners, introducing realistic optical noise, paper skew, and digit confusion (e.g. 194B, 0↔O, 5↔S) with calculated confidence scores.
  • Carlos (Digital Portal Agent): Ingests electronic enrollments via REST API schemas with rigorous header validations.
  • Priya (Intake Quality Gatekeeper): Validates 11-character MBI syntax against CMS standards, checks in-county service area ZIP contracts, and flags demographic defects prior to federal clearinghouse dispatch.
  • CMS Gateway (Federal Adjudication Agent): Evaluates Part A/B entitlements, duplicate enrollment detection, and generates ANSI ASC X12 EDI 834 & MARx Record 61 clearinghouse records.
  • Raj (Work Basket Exception Agent): Resolves operational exceptions under strict CMS 10-day Turnaround Time (TAT) compliance using Highest-Aged Pick Rule (FIFO). Forensically repairs OCR distortions and remaps out-of-area plans to compliant packages.
  • Nora (Statutory Member Correspondence): Generates legally binding CMS model notices complying with 42 CFR §422.568 and §423.568 with statutory 60-day appeal deadlines and SHIP advocacy contacts.
  • Inspector (Cryptographic Compliance Auditor): Independent auditor certifying zero-tolerance quality gates and verifying SHA-256 block hash chaining across the ledger.

FIFO Aging Discipline and the 10-Day Cliff

Under federal guidelines, letting an application sit in a queue past 10 days triggers immediate audit non-compliance. Our work basket queue sorts items strictly by age descending: Day 9–10 items (Critical SLA Risk) are pulled first before newer submissions.

Explore the live application and cryptographic audit ledger at mediflow.kprsnt.in or view the source repository at github.com/kprsnt2/enrolloment-agy-new.
